analysis: Two files changed. (1) .github/workflows/docs-impact.yml adds `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` to the docs-impact checkout (line ~43 on head). The workflow triggers on `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`. It already ran PR-controlled scripts from the merge ref, and fork PRs get a read-only token with no secrets. Checking out the head SHA therefore adds no privilege or secret exposure. The base SHA is still passed through DOCS_IMPACT_BASE, and fetch-depth 0 is kept. GitHub Actions and CI are out of the threat model's scope and no listed asset, boundary or threat is affected. (2) CHANGELOG.md adds one entry under provider 0.9.17 saying an explicitly configured TMPDIR is honored for anonymous runtime metallib snapshots, with unlink-before-copy and digest binding preserved and no fallback on failure. It is a documentation-only change; the provider source implementing it was not supplied. Relevant context for later passes is T-050 (temp-file plaintext exposure) and T-013/T-034 (binary and runtime integrity). A user-controlled TMPDIR for runtime snapshots could be a local tampering surface, but the digest binding and no-fallback behavior in the entry mitigate that, and there is nothing to verify without the code. No security regressions are evident from the supplied changes. Coverage limit: the actual TMPDIR implementation is not in this batch.
